contracts.docstring: Construct routes without inference, database writes or maintenance jobs.
Reject retired implicit setup through the compatibility guard; explicit owner source operations replace initialization, cloning and automatic remote creation.
One exact observed project Stop intent; caller identities/grants and arbitrary target lists are forbidden.
Delete an explicitly selected unused project; execution history and registered workers must be preserved and reconciled instead.
Hold the admission write lock while checking history and removing only an unused project's metadata; source files are never deleted here.
Withdraw this project's native work and request legacy teardown where present; paused describes owner intent, not unproved physical closure.
Original owner selection with no shell commands, caller credentials, namespace identities or fabricated task IDs.
Exact observed administrative target; a stale browser cannot stop a later reconciliation fence.
Save and schedule exactly one explicit source operation; native turns, implicit remote creation and force pushes are outside this request.
Observe this exact saved intent and current local handle without fetching remotes, probing Git or choosing a newest operation.
Withdraw the observed source attempt and drain its actual local owner before acknowledging any verified local closure.
Request readonly reconciliation of the original retained directory and closure; an uncertain effect is never blindly reissued.
Read and archive historical registrations; all source mutations require explicit administrative ownership.
Reject retired setup before filesystem, Git, remote, credential or registration effects; use an original explicit administrative source operation.
Reject retired setup before filesystem, Git, remote, credential or registration effects; use an original explicit administrative source operation.
Reject retired setup before filesystem, Git, remote, credential or registration effects; use an original explicit administrative source operation.
Reject retired setup before filesystem, Git, remote, credential or registration effects; use an original explicit administrative source operation.
Bind explicit authenticated cloning to one configured HTTPS origin without sending its credential to a public or redirected destination.
One exact original source request and fixed Git stage; neither callers nor a model can supply push/config/reset/cleanup arguments.
Match the complete argv/cwd/allocation profile before any shared broker reservation or command gate.
Describe only required original create/clone/read stages; checkout-index without force preserves unexpectedly existing files.
Networking belongs only to the explicitly requested fixed HTTPS clone; observations and checkout keep sockets disabled.
Mount only the original readonly administrative view and private allocation; optional clone networking belongs to fixed trusted Git, not model code.
Use only host-inspected DNS/TLS assets, with no ambient OAuth/PAT, arbitrary helper or user-supplied trust bypass.
Keep the configured PAT out of argv/manifests/config by reading a sealed private credential only inside the exact clone namespace.
Share network only with the exact trusted clone program; this is program confinement, not a kernel destination ACL.
Retain protected-peer and namespace protections while permitting outbound sockets solely for the clone stage.
Pin the host-selected public CA/resolver only for HTTPS; source/control/credential directories are never broadly exposed.
Retain sealed trust/credential descriptors through the original gated spawn, then close them with the owning capsule.
Expose semantic fixed stages while reusing original owned Git transport, complete capture and physical closure.
Bind actual operation/owner/views once; this object has no generic command or native run API.
Launch at most one peer for this original stage; replay returns its receipt rather than silently reissuing an effect.
Capture an actual Git root/complete HEAD/tree/branch/status/origin without converting local credentials or a label into authority.
Retain one real administrative kernel domain through every fixed command and verified retirement, using the shared global concession.
Execute an original local-create/adopt/clone intent, registering only after original domain closure; exact completed retry starts nothing.
Recover original closure then observe only retained Git state in a fresh readonly domain; never repeat init/commit/clone or claim remote server termination.
Keep branch names unambiguous within fixed setup commands without accepting Git options, traversal or reserved HEAD.
An explicit administrative effect scope; adoption cannot secretly initialize Git and clone cannot provision or reconfigure a remote.
Reject ambiguous effects, unsafe names/refs and credential-bearing URLs before persisting or allocating anything.
A captured administrative directory view, deliberately without a fabricated native repository or task identity.
Capture an ordinary non-redirected directory; subsequent controls must match these original kernel identities.
Reuse the existing source identity check without inventing a native registration for this administrative view.
One original administrative owner/fence; no native RunSpec, AttemptLease, model permission or synthetic task is conferred.
Complete point-in-time Git observations from fixed owned commands; not a permanent-health, semantic-acceptance or publication assertion.
Require full same-format objects and avoid persisting credential-bearing origin URLs into project metadata or owner responses.
Persist bounded original setup intents and directory ownership through the existing SQLite/project-metadata transaction.
Use the actual host source policy and private control root; merely constructing or reading this store creates no files or workers.
Reuse the existing database path/device/inode identity rather than deriving authority from a copied database's labels.
Preserve all unrelated project metadata and refuse malformed state instead of treating lost operation history as empty.
Retain administrative operations across project deletion decisions, including completed or uncertain setup history.
Expose complete recorded source intentions and point-in-time observations without peer internals or an implied fresh Git check.
Reject ordinary registration or another setup overlapping an unresolved original destination under the same admission lock.
Read exactly this project and its durable operation collection; a foreign or removed project is never recreated.
Write the complete existing metadata object under the caller's original write lock, retaining owner creation and other domains.
Return a source operation from its exact project/key without a newest-operation fallback.
Read original intent and current saved phase; this does not observe Git, contact remotes or authorize retry.
Read the complete bounded setup history of one project; no partial list is represented as proof of no work.
Validate source scope/reservations under the admission write lock without creating a folder, initializing Git or replacing a registration.
Persist one exact owner intent before any effect; replay returns it, while a reused key with different scope rejects.
Require the original administrative owner/fence and database identity before any directory or peer control.
Give one actual administrative process owner its own attempt/fence, without a native task or model invocation.
Fence an already-closed original attempt and retain its history before a new strictly readonly reconciliation; never restart its writes.
Capture one original directory allocation before Git; a partial unrecorded folder is retained and never erased or guessed to be ours.
Retain the original physical domain before a setup command can be launched; another domain cannot replace an uncertain attempt.
Register the actually observed directory only after original global domain closure, preserving any already-matching registration without rewriting metadata.
Retain an interrupted/failed operation and its original directories/peers; absence of a reply does not authorize another Git write.
Expose a bounded redacted current issue while retaining the original operation, physical receipts and any partial files for explicit observation.
Withdraw admission for exactly the observed administrative fence; a stale Stop cannot target a new reconciliation attempt.
Withdraw one original source inside either the individual Stop or atomic whole-project Stop admission transaction.
Record stopped only after original local closure, retaining partially written folders and uncertainty instead of asserting a remote effect was undone.
Bind the complete original request, operator configuration and captured directory views across all command stages.
Adapt the existing host broker protocol to a real administrative operation; no repository/task/run identity is fabricated.
Freeze one original source lease and fixed command stage; recovered instances may project closure but never prepare another stage.
Retain one peer per original stage so response loss cannot mint another write under a different peer identity.
Read only an exact peer of this operation; labels from a native task cannot authorize it.
Recheck actual owner/root/allocation and original stage before the shared broker can reserve its global concession.
Persist the actual namespace identity before the broker releases G; there is no user-supplied PID or closure flag.
Project only the broker's witnessed closure for this administrative origin; a native closure or caller boolean cannot complete source setup.
Own actual administrative worker handles without inventing native turns or replaying interrupted writes after restart.
Reuse the serving runtime's original host configuration, store, owner lock and kernel broker boundaries.
Pass only actual host-owned launcher settings; no model, user argv or caller credential supplies execution authority.
Expose saved phase and actual local worker observation; a stopped local worker never proves remote rollback or fresh Git health.
Persist exact owner intent before scheduling one bounded worker; an original replay returns history and never restarts a stopped or uncertain effect.
Start only explicit readonly reconciliation of the retained operation; no implicit clone, initialization, commit or credentialed write is replayed.
Keep executor teardown in its owning task and retain failures as saved uncertainty; raw transport errors and secrets never enter the owner response.
Wait for the exact current local handle, without replaying work if its process or application has gone away.
Withdraw exact observed admission before cancelling its original local worker; preserve unconfirmed closure if that handle is absent.
Withdraw all currently recorded administrative work for the legacy bodyless project Stop, preserving uncertain original effects when no live handle exists.
Withdraw all owned source jobs before the runtime releases its exclusive store owner lock; cancellation is issued once and closure is drained.
Drain the original physical handle even if persistence is unavailable during shutdown; no other job is skipped after an error.
Compose attributed current evidence and atomically save a separate owner decision in the existing receipt transaction, without inference or Git.
Recompute all project scope and current original evidence; a previous report cannot silently stand in for changed requirements or work.
Render exact attributed material and concrete interpretation limits; never summarize away source constraints or invent semantic fulfillment.
Project real saved state without treating metadata as activity/closure or inventing a plan choice; no model, Git, remote setup or second coordinator.
Freeze only original active/uncertain runs and active graph authorizations; closed reviewable proposals remain intact.
Read directory-policy observations, metadata and exact historical links without probing Git/remotes or selecting an arbitrary newest plan.
Register only an existing directory under the real managed root; same resource intent returns the original ID without Git/init/clone/origin/network effects.
Atomically pause exactly observed graphs and withdraw exactly observed run authority before acknowledging intent; replay never retargets new work or claims closure.

One externally supplied, non-reused domain for one original attempt.

``run_peer`` owns reserve→spawn→global publication→concrete local bind→G.
Callers receive a transport only after G and can only recover a receipt on
retry. ``revoke`` withdraws G before waiting for SQL/constructors. Global
recovery needs only the journal/domain, never the original project DB.
Complete actor-origin and endpoint authentication remain deployment work.
Bind original physical ownership and optional operator remote configuration before any peer or credential is admitted.
Retain one immutable source concession and record each operation's actual execution view.
Witness launch intent and manifests before releasing the original gate.
Project witnessed closure into its original native or administrative registry; source labels never transfer authority between the two domains.
Own native attempts and grant-bound tool closure before durable terminal states.
Compose one journal owner, native worker limits and deterministic authorized-plan dispatch; construction starts no work.
Lazily compose administrative source workers from actual owned runtime configuration; construction launches no Git or model work.
Drain dispatcher admissions before withdrawing workers and releasing the journal owner lock.
Withdraw every active native run in this project; returned states preserve unconfirmed physical closure rather than claiming all work stopped.
Observe administrative history even after this process restarted without reactivating or replaying its worker.
Resolve actual registered source identities under one host root; names and paths are data, never execution authority.
Apply the same source identity/root/overlap policy inside an original owner registration transaction, without Git or filesystem mutation.
Validate an existing source directory before registration as well as admission, sharing the same host-root/database/foreign-project overlap policy.
Construct the historical record reader without Git, remote configuration or process side effects.
Restored metadata can be browsed without recreating its repositories, remotes or old initialization effects.
Archiving historical metadata never cleans the source folder or deletes retained work.
Old callers must adopt explicit administrative ownership instead of receiving an automatic remote or an unowned Git process.
The retained tool cannot grant itself authority by manufacturing a path or using ambient Forgejo settings.
Late preparation cannot cross a corrected context; its useful files and closure evidence survive.
Model the owner correcting requirements after the physical clone has already finished.
Inspect only the test-owned source from the host to independently verify the setup result and preservation.
A real initial revision is usable through source admission, exact replay launches nothing, and adoption preserves dirty files/config/origin.
Losing the DB registration after a real initial commit must not reinitialize, recommit or replace the retained source on repair.
Inject the exact crash gap after Git/domain closure but before any resource registration transaction.
An explicitly authenticated fixed clone uses real local TLS/Git reads, never a remote creation/push, and retains one original source after completed retry.
An administrative source intent is real outstanding project work even without a native task; a historical owner decision cannot close it by replay.
Use this real isolated project store and actual host root; no process, model or remote is created by the storage fixture.
Same original scope yields one operation; changing it cannot reuse that identity or start a second intent.
Creating is not adopting; reservations cannot overlap another project's existing source or another uncompleted setup intent.
One live setup owner captures a new private directory and a distinct readonly view without a synthetic native repository binding.
Adoption does not initialize/configure a source or discard the owner's immutable creation metadata.
Remote intent is explicit and credential-free; a clone cannot request a visibility change or use an embedded PAT.
An administrative intent retains its recovery identity and partially allocated directory even without native run history.
The actual owner route creates one source asynchronously, while exact replay retains its registration and never creates a native task.
Stopping after init withdraws the original administrative attempt, proves its local domain closure and preserves the unfinished source on exit.
Pause the actual worker between fixed Git stages, after real init/peer closure and before any commit effect.
The UI receives a redacted saved uncertainty and can explicitly recover the actual existing initial revision through the owner observation endpoint.
Lose the actual registration reply after Git completed; this private detail must not enter the owner response.
The real owner clone uses its configured credential origin and CA, independently of the model runtime's public-network trust configuration.
A useful existing directory and its recorded source survive every retired setup route without a subprocess, remote call or metadata rewrite.
Abort the first unowned process before the legacy implementation can modify even the isolated fixture.
A source cleanup failure propagates only after the actual coordinator has withdrawn and drained its already-registered native adapter worker.
Model only the source family reporting failed SQL persistence after it drained its own physical handles.
Report an original source-receipt failure; this must not prevent independent native worker teardown.
An in-flight preparation cannot enqueue an administrative worker after source shutdown took its final handle snapshot and released store ownership.
Hold the actual admission handoff before its real transaction, without starting Git or fabricating closure evidence.
Represent a registered finite worker handle only; no process, lease, file or model is created in this admission-order test.
Observe the real source shutdown boundary; finishing before admission drains demonstrates the ownership defect.
Historical argument compatibility only; these fields cannot authorize source or remote effects.
Retained compatibility entry point that explains the explicit owner setup replacement without executing it.
Reject model-origin repository setup; an owner must choose its exact directory, mode and original intent through source controls.

scope: New/changed Python definitions and modules in this delivery. Relevant new frontend modules and exported helpers also carry English JSDoc; no claim that all historic project definitions are documented.
